doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: The 1956 European tour
summary: Two months in Europe: work permit delay, touring by Opel, playing in Koblenz, Paris, Venice and Holland.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We had a very interesting trip through Europe. Well first of all we were over there for two months. We got off the ship and we had an engagement already arranged in Holland. But that got delayed because we needed work permits and we didn’t have them. So that was the better part of July that we were involved there, and then around the first of August we rented two Opals and toured around. We went all the way down into Italy and back up through Germany and back to Holland. And then we got back on the boat and came back in September.
Were you playing on those tours?

We had quite a few engagements. The Army hired us in Koblenz. We played on street corners in Paris and got arrested. We played on the Grand Canal in Venice and the police came along and said, “Please would you move to the next obelisk because you’re disturbing the symphony orchestra in the main square.” But we just had a hat on the floor. And then when we got back to Holland we were asked to go to a hotel up in the very north of Holland. And we played for teenagers in the afternoon and then played for adults in the evening and the owner of the hotel put us up for the night and paid our train fare back and forth, and we got a little pay. So but the stint in Europe, in Holland that is, was two weeks. And that was really the only formal engagement we had lined up before we went.
And the thing at Carnegie Hall was when you came back?
When we came back it was the following November.
